evals.name: research-reading-handout
evals.prompt: Compile these tart cherry research notes into a readable PDF handout for me. Condense until I can read it in 15 minutes or less. I'm a cyclist training 15+ hours per week and want a practical guide to dosing and timing, including what a 4.8x concentrate label does and doesn't tell me. No bibliography. Use only the supplied sources; no fresh research. Save the finished PDF in the specified output directory, not my Inbox. Do not print.
evals.expected_output: A comfortable, coherent reading handout with a practical dosing/timing comparison table, accurate treatment of concentrate equivalence and evidence limitations, and no bibliography. Readability, whitespace, and graphics are evaluated by human review.
assertions: The delivered handout is a nonempty PDF with A4 pages (portrait or landscape).
Composed text uses embedded fonts; included source pages are evaluated separately.
Composed pages have no footers, page-number footers, eyebrows, sidenote headers, or sidenote rules.
The handout has no bibliography or source-reference apparatus.
A readable comparison table groups the use cases with their doses and timing, rather than presenting every protocol only as prose.
The handout distinguishes loading/continued dosing from a single immediate post-ride dose.
The handout does not assert that a 4.8x concentration ratio establishes polyphenol content or exact equivalence to the studied concentrate.
Extracted reading text contains no more than 3000 words (15 minutes at 200 words/minute).
On composed pages, all main-content text, headings, tables, calendars, figures, and captions stay inside the prose column, without entering the gutter or sidenote column or spanning both columns.

evals.name: flight-options-comparison
evals.prompt: Prepare a PDF handout comparing all six family flight options in the supplied files. Start with a calendar graphic comparing the options and an all-in cost table. For each option include the flight table, a small calendar, full days in each place, extra workdays, and flying versus total journey time. Put these facts in consistent locations so I can compare them easily. Explain the added costs and separate-ticket risks plainly. No new flight searches and no QR codes or invented links. Use only the supplied data. Save the finished PDF in the specified output directory, not my Inbox. Do not print.
evals.expected_output: A printable comparison with six complete options, accurate costs/dates/day counts, legible calendars and tables, and consistent option panels. The supplied itineraries are fictional, frozen layout-test data.
assertions: The delivered handout is a nonempty PDF with A4 pages (portrait or landscape).
Composed text uses embedded fonts; included source pages are evaluated separately.
Composed pages have no footers, page-number footers, eyebrows, sidenote headers, or sidenote rules.
All six options A–F appear with correct family totals: A $7920, B $7430, C $7730, D $7270, E $7690, F $6356.
Options A–C show four extra workdays and D–F show three; Boston full days are A/B seven and C–F six; every option has six Colorado full days.
Each option shows local flight times and distinguishes flying from total journey time, including the four-hour drive where applicable.
An opening comparison calendar and option-level calendars are present.
Option F discloses the separate-ticket SFO bag reclaim/recheck and unprotected missed-connection risk.
On composed pages, all main-content text, headings, tables, calendars, figures, and captions stay inside the prose column, without entering the gutter or sidenote column or spanning both columns.
